questions.q: What does the Service Value System (SVS) describe, overall?
options: A single software tool organizations must purchase
How all of an organization's components and activities work together to enable value creation from opportunity and demand
Only the incident management practice
A replacement name for the ITIL certification exam
questions.explain: The SVS is the overall model for how an organization converts opportunity and demand into value, using all its components together.

questions.q: What are the five components of the Service Value System?
options: Guiding Principles, Governance, the Service Value Chain, Practices, and Continual Improvement
Service Strategy, Service Design, Service Transition, Service Operation, and CSI
Incident, Problem, Change, Request, and Knowledge management
Plan, Build, Run, Monitor, and Retire
questions.explain: These five components are the SVS; the five-stage list is the earlier ITIL v3 lifecycle, not the SVS.

questions.q: What is the Service Value Chain (SVC), per this lesson?
options: A fixed, one-way sequence of steps every organization must follow in order
The operational core of the SVS: six interconnected activities that convert demand into value, combinable in different orders depending on the situation
A list of the 34 ITIL 4 practices
Another name for Governance
questions.explain: The SVC's six activities — Plan, Improve, Engage, Design & Transition, Obtain/Build, and Deliver & Support — are deliberately not a fixed sequence.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe Continual Improvement within the SVS?
options: It only applies at the very end of a project, as a final review
It is unrelated to Guiding Principles or Governance
It is both a specific practice and a thread that runs through every other SVS component continuously
It replaced Governance in ITIL 4
questions.explain: Continual Improvement is explicitly described as running through the whole system, not confined to one phase or component.

questions.q: What is the real shift this lesson identifies between ITIL v3 and the ITIL 4 Service Value System?
options: ITIL 4 removed the need for any documented practices
Moving from a lifecycle you move through stage by stage to a system you operate continuously, with all parts active at once
ITIL 4 reduced the framework down to a single component
There is no meaningful difference between the two models
questions.explain: The SVS's components operate together continuously, rather than being traversed in sequence the way the v3 lifecycle stages were.
